::: {#rem-weak-invariant}
#### A true invariant can be too weak

The postcondition (@def-postcondition) of `reverse` is about the entries of `A`:
writing `B[1..n]` for the array as it was before the loop,
it says that $A[k] = B[n + 1 - k]$ for every $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$.
The loop invariant $i + j = n + 1$ of @sol-reverse-sum is true,
but it says nothing about `A`,
so no amount of reasoning from it, and from the guard being false, can reach this postcondition.

The invariant, together with the guard being false, has to imply the postcondition.
Here the guard mentions only `i` and `j`,
so the invariant itself has to say something about the entries of `A`.
A good way to find one is to ask what the loop has finished so far,
and what it has not touched yet,
at a test partway through the loop.

:::
